---
name: horizon
description: How to work inside an Archon Horizon workspace — orient from on-disk state, pick the highest-value formalization work, record progress as commits, and coordinate. Load this first; it points to the specialized skills for detail. Editable per workspace.
---

You are working inside an **Archon Horizon** workspace: a place where AI agents
formalize mathematics in Lean 4 across one or more projects. This skill is the
map. It is deliberately short and **you can edit it** (it lives at
`.claude/skills/horizon/SKILL.md` in this workspace) — tune it to how you want to
work. It points to focused skills; load those on demand rather than up front.

## You are a team; the workspace is where teams collaborate

Think of your session as **one team**: you (the lead) plus the subagents you
spawn as your **workers**, with the tools and skills available to you. A
`horizon run` is your team working through its task. Other runs are **other
teams** working in parallel on the *same shared workspace* — one Lean project set,
one roadmap/board, one ledger, one inbox.

You do not manage other teams and they do not manage you. You coordinate through
**shared state**, not meetings:

- **The board (roadmap)** is the shared plan. Keep your items' status/owner/
  milestone current so other teams see what you hold and where it's going.
- **The inbox** is asynchronous messaging + memory across teams (skill:
  `horizon-inbox`): shared notes, per-task private items, and direct messages to
  another team.
- **Commits** are the durable record; reading recent ledger history tells you what
  other teams just produced (skill: `project-git`).

Before you start, be aware of who else is live (see "Is another run live" below).
A short **synchronizer** digest is printed to stderr at the start of your CLI
commands. Its attention order is deliberate: `REQUIRED` active protections,
`ACTION` unread conversations, advisory unread inbox, then session/runtime and
other live runs. Read it; it is how you stay aware without asking anyone. A new
conversation or reply invalidates the digest cache immediately. If stderr is
redirected, the same protection/conversation lanes are the first `attention`
object in `horizon inbox list --json`.

## Orient (pull state, don't assume it)

**Start here:** your prompt says nothing about who ran before you. Usually
somebody did — often minutes ago, often on this same task, and their report was
written for you. Skill: `horizon-start` — one cheap pass that works out which
situation you were launched into (fresh run, hand-off from the session that just
finished, resume after a crash, or outside a run) and what to read for each.

The workspace root is `$ARCHON_HORIZON_ROOT`; your shell may start in a member
project rather than at that root. The absolute path to this skill is
`$ARCHON_HORIZON_SKILL`. Live state is under
`$ARCHON_HORIZON_ROOT/.archon-horizon/` and the manifest is
`$ARCHON_HORIZON_ROOT/config.yaml`. Read what you need, when you need it — via the
`horizon` CLI (invoke it as `"$HORIZON_BIN" …`):

- **Roadmap** — YOUR strategy sketch across *all* projects, kept as a nested
  outline. `"$HORIZON_BIN" roadmap list` renders the indented tree with per-parent
  progress (`active · 3/7 done`); `--focus <id>` shows one subtree, `--max-depth 0`
  the top level only. Structure it: nest sub-goals with `--parent`, keep your
  item's status/strategy current as you work. It doubles as the **project board**:
  set `--owner <team>` (who holds it), `--milestone <label>` (a free grouping tag,
  filter with `roadmap list --milestone <label>`), and pin concrete deliverables
  with `--pin-commit <sha>`. Roadmap commands print a **warning**
  when parent/child statuses disagree (all sub-items done but parent open, or a
  done parent with open children) — nothing is auto-corrected; you decide whether
  to fix it or leave it (it may be intentional). They also warn when too many
  milestones claim simultaneous `active` focus.
- **Tasks** — a specific piece of work, usually the one a human launched and is
  watching. `"$HORIZON_BIN" task …`. Task commands warn when the open queue grows
  beyond the advisory limit or a `running` status looks orphaned.
- **Inbox** — how teams talk across sessions and projects. Leave a note for the
  next session; read what past ones left. `"$HORIZON_BIN" inbox …` (skill:
  `horizon-inbox`). Items can be **owned by your task** (private, e.g. your team's
  memory) or **shared with everyone** (the default); read-state is per-team, so
  `inbox list --mine --unread` is your team's fresh queue, and you can
  direct-message another team with `--to task:<id>`. Inbox commands warn when the
  open working set—especially `memory` and `info`—needs review.
- **Inbox attention order** — before edits, inspect all open `protection` items
  (standing constraints, whether read or unread), then open unread
  `conversation` items and reply or mark them read. Other kinds are advisory
  context. In an agent session an unqualified `inbox list` defaults to open items
  and sorts in this order; use an explicit status to audit history.
- **Conversation discipline** — use a conversation only when a reply/decision is
  expected. Search and reuse an open thread before starting one. Its initiator is
  a participant and owns closure: after consuming the answer, add a concise
  conclusion if needed and archive the thread. Reply to human-started threads but
  leave their closure to the human unless asked otherwise (skill: `horizon-inbox`).
- **Blueprint graph** — declaration dependencies and what's proved. `"$HORIZON_BIN" graph -p <project> …` (skill: `hgraph`).
  Each node is also an **hgraph** file with attached comments/reviews —
  `"$HORIZON_BIN" graph -p <project> frontier` ranks what to prove next, and node-scoped failure memory
  goes on the node itself (skill: `hgraph`).
- **Memory** — durable facts/dead-ends live in the inbox: read with
  `"$HORIZON_BIN" inbox list --kind memory --json`, write with
  `"$HORIZON_BIN" inbox add --kind memory --to horizon --body …`.
- **Usage** — your token/cost consumption this session and run, budget headroom,
  and recent rate-limit signals: `"$HORIZON_BIN" usage --json`. See
  "Pace yourself" below for how to act on it.

## Your session's identity (environment variables)

The harness exports these to every session — read them instead of guessing:

| Variable | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `ARCHON_HORIZON_ROOT` | workspace root (use for `--root`-free CLI calls) |
| `ARCHON_HORIZON_SKILL` | absolute path to this `SKILL.md` (never resolve it relative to the shell cwd) |
| `ARCHON_HORIZON_RUN` | run id (e.g. `0163`) |
| `ARCHON_HORIZON_SESSION` | this session's name (e.g. `0002-horizon-T-1`) |
| `ARCHON_HORIZON_SESSION_DIR` | this session's directory (transcript, usage.json, report) |
| `ARCHON_HORIZON_ROUND` / `ARCHON_HORIZON_ROUNDS` | which round this is (0-based) / the run's planned total |
| `ARCHON_HORIZON_TASK` / `ARCHON_HORIZON_TASK_TITLE` | the task id / title (full body: `"$HORIZON_BIN" task show "$ARCHON_HORIZON_TASK" --json`) |
| `ARCHON_HORIZON_PROJECTS` | comma-separated projects this task spans |
| `HORIZON_BIN`, `HORIZON_GIT` | absolute paths to the CLI and the ledger-git wrapper |
| `HORIZON_LEDGER_GIT_DIR`, `HORIZON_LEDGER_WORK_TREE` | the workspace ledger repo + its work tree — `"$HORIZON_GIT" …` is shorthand for `git --git-dir "$HORIZON_LEDGER_GIT_DIR" --work-tree "$HORIZON_LEDGER_WORK_TREE" …` |

## Pace yourself (usage & interruption risk)

Sessions end for reasons you don't control: rate limits, usage caps, budgets.
The defense is NOT to avoid work — it is to make interruption cheap:

- **Commit at every coherent point** (plain git into the ledger, below). If
  `"$HORIZON_BIN" usage --json` shows low budget headroom or recent
  `rate_limit`/`usage_limit` signals, commit what you have NOW and prefer
  finishing the piece in flight over opening a new front.
- If this is the run's **last round** (`ARCHON_HORIZON_ROUND` + 1 ==
  `ARCHON_HORIZON_ROUNDS`), leave the workspace hand-off-clean: commit, update
  the roadmap/task status, and write the report as if nobody continues today.
- Interrupted anyway? Nothing is lost that was committed — the next session
  resumes from the ledger (see "Resuming" below).

## One-shot discipline (important)

This session runs to completion and is **not resumed** — you will not be re-invoked
when a background job finishes. So **run work in the foreground and block on it**
(builds, checks, subagents). Anything you leave running in the background, or leave
uncommitted, may be lost when the session ends. Commit early and often (below).

## Pick the highest-value work

Read the roadmap and the live Lean state, then commit to the most valuable next
piece. A node being large, multi-session, or blocked on missing mathlib
infrastructure is **not** a reason to skip it — start it, build the missing
lemma/definition yourself as project-local infrastructure, and push it as far as
you genuinely can. Prefer ambitious progress over defensive avoidance.

If this session was launched on a specific task, make concrete progress on that
task's REAL objective — don't preemptively pivot to easy unrelated wins because
the objective is large. Leave a concise task comment only for a durable state
change or blocker, not every action. You own the task's terminal status (skill:
`task-status`): set `--status done` only when the objective is FULLY complete;
`blocked`/`failed` if genuinely stuck; set nothing if it's only partly advanced
(it returns to the queue).

## Fresh-context checkpoints

The old Ground pass is no longer a second orchestrator role, but independent
review is still part of convergence. Spawn the **`ground`** subagent at these
checkpoints:

- before marking a multi-step task `done`;
- after every two substantive Horizon sessions on a long-running task;
- immediately after a strategy pivot, a broad workspace edit, or a surprising
  clean/build result.

Give it the task/project scope and ask it to inspect the actual ledger diff,
blueprint graph, Lean state, roadmap, inbox, and reports with fresh context. It
is read-only on source and reports issues/memory; reconcile its findings before
continuing. Use **`work-reviewer`** for a narrow diff/proof audit and **`janitor`**
when the main concern is workspace hygiene. A one-session task may skip the
periodic checkpoint, but must still obtain a fresh-context review before a
terminal `done` claim.

Schedule upkeep even when the last command did not print a warning. On a
multi-session run, dispatch **`janitor` at the start of every second Horizon
session** and before the final report; on a one-session task, dispatch it once
before claiming completion if the run touched roadmap, task, or inbox state.
Record the checkpoint in the report and wait for the helper before continuing.
If `janitor` is unavailable, ask **`ground`** for the same hygiene inspection;
Ground is read-only, so apply or explicitly record its findings yourself.

## Warnings are work

Commands report problems for a reason — never scroll past them. `lake build`
warnings, `horizon graph sync` warnings, roadmap consistency warnings, deprecation
notices from any tool: if your change caused it, **fix it now** (it is part of
the task); if it's pre-existing or caused by the tool/command itself, don't
silently ignore it — record it as a memory item, file an inbox `issue`, or
address it `--to human` when a human decision is needed. A warning that
survives your session should be one you *chose* to leave, with a trace saying
why.

Collection-health warnings are a dispatch trigger, not background noise. When
`inbox`, `roadmap`, or `task` reports an overloaded queue, stale running item,
or status mismatch, pause the proof loop and spawn **`janitor`** with the
workspace scope. Wait for it, reconcile its report, rerun the command, and
record any warning that remains intentionally. Do this at most once for the
same warning in a session; a persistent warning still needs a report or inbox
issue rather than repeated no-op calls.

## Do the work (Lean)

hgraph
horizon

horizon-start
horizon-waiting
lean-check
leansearch

---
name: project-git
description: How git works in an Archon Horizon workspace — one out-of-tree workspace ledger (no per-project repos); read a project's history by pathspec or by a session's commit trailers.
---

Read this before running `git diff`/`git log` on a project.

## The model

- **One out-of-tree workspace ledger.** Archon commits to a single repo whose git
  dir is `.archon-horizon/vcs/workspace.git` with the workspace **root** as its
  work tree (driven via `--git-dir`/`--work-tree`). `<root>/.git` is deliberately
  untouched — it is reserved for a user repo. The ledger records one commit per
  completed session: `config.yaml`, the session's scoped project files, and
  `.archon-horizon/` shared state; never the binary git dirs under
  `.archon-horizon/vcs/`, locks, or other volatile internals.
- **There are no per-project repositories.** A project directory has no nested
  `.git/`, and there is no `.archon-horizon/vcs/<project>.git`. A project's
  "history" is simply the workspace ledger filtered to that project's path.
- **You record your own work by committing to the ledger** with plain `git` (see
  below). Commit after each independently useful, verified proof/file/tooling
  change, before a long build or delegated review, and before expanding scope.
  A multi-hour implementation session should normally have several commits; one
  commit is appropriate only when the work is genuinely atomic. The message +
  diff is how progress is read, so use a semantic, math-first subject. Provenance
  trailers are added automatically; do not write them.

So a plain `git diff` at the root sees only a user repo (if any), never Archon's.
Drive the out-of-tree workspace ledger explicitly (or use `hgit`).

## Recording your work (committing)

Commits go to the ledger, **not** to `<root>/.git` and **not** via any project
`.git` (there is none). Do **not** `export GIT_DIR` / `GIT_WORK_TREE` yourself — that
would redirect `lake` and other tooling. Two equivalent ways to commit:

```bash
# 1) The `hgit` wrapper (on the session env as $HORIZON_GIT) — plain git, ledger-scoped:
"$HORIZON_GIT" add path/to/File.lean
"$HORIZON_GIT" commit -m "feat(chapter): prove foo_lemma" \
  --trailer 'Summary=**Proof.** Closed the compactness step using $K \subseteq X$.'

# 2) The explicit form (identical effect):
git --git-dir="$HORIZON_LEDGER_GIT_DIR" --work-tree="$HORIZON_LEDGER_WORK_TREE" \
    add path/to/File.lean
git --git-dir="$HORIZON_LEDGER_GIT_DIR" --work-tree="$HORIZON_LEDGER_WORK_TREE" \
    commit -m "feat(chapter): prove foo_lemma" \
    --trailer 'Summary=**Proof.** Closed the compactness step using $K \subseteq X$.'
```

Ordinary git: the ledger's index tracks HEAD, so `add` then `commit` records your
files on top of it. Horizon's own commits stage in a private index and never leave
anything staged in your way.

- **Prefer the pathspec commit** — name the paths on the commit itself:
  `"$HORIZON_GIT" commit -m "…" --trailer 'Summary=…' -- path/to/File.lean`
  It records exactly those files, ignores whatever else may be staged, and git
  builds its tree from the **current** HEAD — so it cannot silently revert a
  concurrent session's files the way a commit built on a stale index can.
- Add at least one **`Summary` trailer** explaining the important change, not
  merely repeating the subject. Use one trailer per distinct explanation when
  useful. Its value supports Markdown and LaTeX, so concise mathematical context
  such as `--trailer 'Summary=**Invariant.** Preserves $f(x)=x$ on $A$.'` renders
  directly in the dashboard commit item. Keep each trailer on one line; repeat
  `--trailer 'Summary=…'` for a few separate points.
- Do not wait for the whole task to be complete. A checkpoint commit must build
  or otherwise be internally coherent, but it may explicitly leave the next
  named obligation open.
- Stage **explicit paths** you changed rather than `add -A` — the work tree is the
  whole workspace, so `-A` can sweep in unrelated files.
- `Archon-Run`/`Session`/`Role`/`Task`/`Projects` trailers are stamped for you by a
  hook from the session env; your message stays clean.
- Build artifacts (`.lake`, `*.olean`, …) are excluded automatically, and any
  high-confidence credential is **redacted to `XXXX`** in the staged content (not
  blocked), so a broad add still won't leak a secret into the ledger.
- If the guard reports *"redacted possible secret(s) to XXXX"*, it scrubbed a
  matched credential and let the commit through — **rotate the real credential**,
  and check you didn't stage more than you meant to (`ARCHON_HORIZON_ALLOW_SECRETS=1`
  skips the scan entirely). A *separate* guard still **blocks** a commit that would
  silently delete tracked files you didn't change (a stale-index clobber); re-seed
  the index (`git read-tree HEAD && git add -- <your files>`) rather than forcing it.

Then verify **in the ledger**, and verify the **paths**, not just the SHA — a bare
`git cat-file` runs against `<root>/.git`, which has not seen your commit yet and will
make a perfectly real SHA look fabricated:

```bash
"$HORIZON_GIT" ls-tree --name-only HEAD -- path/to/File.lean   # empty ⇒ NOT in HEAD
```

## Concurrent sessions and the clobber guard

Several sessions may commit to the ledger at once. A commit whose index was
seeded from an older HEAD (e.g. `read-tree`, then a concurrent session commits,
then you commit) produces a tree that *lacks* the other session's new files —
plain git would commit it without any error and silently delete their work.
The ledger's `pre-commit` guard now rejects any commit that stages deletions
you did not ask for:

- *"this commit would DELETE N tracked file(s) you did not change"* — your
  index base is stale (or you are committing through a polluted shared index).
  **Do not override.** Re-seed and retry; your own edits are safe in the
  working tree, which concurrent commits never touch:

  ```bash
  "$HORIZON_GIT" read-tree HEAD
  "$HORIZON_GIT" add -- <your files>
  "$HORIZON_GIT" commit -m "…"          # or just: commit -m "…" -- <your files>
  ```

- Deleting a file **on purpose** (moved/retired): set
  `ARCHON_HORIZON_ALLOW_DELETIONS=1` for that one commit.

At the **end of the session**, re-verify content — not just that HEAD moved —
since a stale-based commit elsewhere could have landed after yours (the guard
blocks new offenders, but belt-and-braces):

```bash
"$HORIZON_GIT" cat-file -e HEAD:path/to/File.lean && \
"$HORIZON_GIT" show HEAD:path/to/File.lean | diff -q - path/to/File.lean
```

If you were clobbered anyway: `read-tree HEAD`, re-add your files from the
working tree, commit once.

## Reading history / a project's diff

Run from the workspace root:

```bash
GD=.archon-horizon/vcs/workspace.git

git --git-dir=$GD --work-tree=. log  --oneline -n 20                       # whole ledger
git --git-dir=$GD --work-tree=. log  --oneline -n 20 -- <project-path>     # one project
git --git-dir=$GD --work-tree=. diff HEAD~1 -- <project-path>
git --git-dir=$GD --work-tree=. diff HEAD~1 -- '<project-path>/*.lean'
git --git-dir=$GD --work-tree=. show <sha>
```

Each commit carries provenance trailers — `Archon-Run`, `Archon-Session`,
`Archon-Role`, `Archon-Task`, `Archon-Projects` — so you can map a commit to the
run/session that made it and see what it touched without parsing prose:

```bash
git --git-dir=$GD --work-tree=. \
  log --format='%H %(trailers:key=Archon-Session,valueonly)' -- <project-path>
```

To see what the previous Horizon agent changed, find its session's commit(s) by
the `Archon-Session` trailer and diff each against **its own parent** (what that
commit changed).

## Caveats

- With parallel runs the ledger is one shared branch: commits from several runs
  interleave, and a commit's parent may belong to another run or a dashboard
  publish. Diff a commit against its own parent (what *that* commit changed), not
  across a span of sessions — that would fold in unrelated runs' changes.
- The bundled author identity is `Archon Horizon <archon-horizon@local>`.

115	/-! ## §1. The cover of a `k`-test by its base change, as an `Over`-morphism -/
116	
117	/-- The base change `T ×_k Spec k'` of a `k`-test `T`, regarded as a `k'`-test
118	via the second projection.
119	
120	This is the object the descent step's classes live on: a class over `k'` is a
121	class on `T_{k'}` for the tests `T` of interest, and `§2` shows a `k`-class is
122	determined by its restriction here. -/
123	noncomputable abbrev baseTest (T : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))) :
124	    Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k')) :=
125	  Over.mk (pullback.snd T.hom (specMapAlgebra k k'))
126	
127	/-- **The covering morphism `T_{k'} ⟶ T`**, in the slice over `Spec k`.
128	
129	Its underlying scheme map is exactly `pullback.fst`, which is the morphism
130	`Picard/EtaleFieldCover.lean` builds its covering sieve from — so the sheaf
131	axiom landed there applies to this morphism on the nose (checked by `rfl`:
132	`coverMap_left`). -/
133	noncomputable def coverMap (T : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))) :
134	    (restrictTest k k').obj (baseTest (k' := k') T) ⟶ T :=
135	  Over.homMk (pullback.fst T.hom (specMapAlgebra k k'))
136	    (pullback.condition (f := T.hom) (g := specMapAlgebra k k'))
137	
138	/-- The cover morphism's underlying scheme map **is** `pullback.fst`, definitionally.
139	
140	This is the identification that lets `§2` feed
141	`Scheme.picEt_ext_of_pullback_agrees`, whose sieve is generated by
142	`Presieve.singleton (pullback.fst T.hom (specMapAlgebra k k'))`. -/
143	@[simp]
144	theorem coverMap_left (T : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))) :
145	    (coverMap (k' := k') T).left = pullback.fst T.hom (specMapAlgebra k k') := rfl
146	
147	/-! ## §2. The uniqueness half of the descent — PROVED -/
148	
149	/-- **Restriction along `T_{k'} ⟶ T` is injective on `picEt`-classes.**
150	
151	For a smooth proper curve `C` over an arbitrary field `k`, an arbitrary finite
152	separable `k'/k`, and an arbitrary `k`-test `T`: two classes in
153	`Pic_{(C/k)ét}(T)` that agree after restriction to `T ×_k Spec k'` are equal.
154	
155	This is the *uniqueness* half of the descent step, and it is what makes a
156	descended class unique once one exists — so `picEtRestrictEquiv_of_surjective`
157	below needs no separate uniqueness hypothesis.
158	
159	**Where the content is, stated precisely.** The amalgamation property itself is
160	free: `Scheme.isSheafFor_picEt_of_mem` holds at *every* covering sieve of
161	`etaleTopologyOver k`, `⊤` included, because it is `PicSharp.etaleSheaf`'s own
162	`Sheaf.cond` pushed through the forgetful functor. What this lemma adds over
163	`Scheme.picEt_ext_of_pullback_agrees` is the reduction from that lemma's
164	*sieve-indexed* hypothesis — agreement after restriction along **every** arrow of
165	the generated sieve — to agreement along the **single** morphism `coverMap`. The
166	step is the factorisation: an arrow of the sieve factors through `pullback.fst`,
167	and lifting that factorisation to the slice over `Spec k` is where
168	`pullback.condition` is consumed.
169	
170	**No hypothesis on `C(k)`** (`I-0491`), and none on `T`. The finite-separability
171	binders are inherited from the covering-sieve membership witness of
172	`Picard/EtaleFieldCover.lean`, which is where they are genuinely used; they are
173	*not* needed by the cross-base identification (`picEt_crossBaseIso` holds for an
174	arbitrary field extension). -/
175	theorem picEt_injective_restrict_baseTest
176	    [FiniteDimensional k k'] [Algebra.IsSeparable k k']
177	    (C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)))
178	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
179	    (T : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)))
180	    {t₁ t₂ : (picEt C).obj (Opposite.op T)}
181	    (h : (picEt C).map (coverMap (k' := k') T).op t₁
182	       = (picEt C).map (coverMap (k' := k') T).op t₂) :
183	    t₁ = t₂ := by
184	  refine AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.picEt_ext_of_pullback_agrees k' C T ?_
185	  intro W g hg
186	  rw [Sieve.overEquiv_symm_iff] at hg
187	  obtain ⟨Z, a, b, hb, hfac⟩ := hg
188	  cases hb
189	  -- `g` factors through `coverMap` in the slice over `Spec k`.
190	  have hgfac : g = (Over.homMk a (by
191	      rw [← Over.w g]
192	      simp only [restrictTest, Over.map_obj_hom, baseTest, Over.mk_hom, ← hfac]
193	      rw [Category.assoc]
194	      exact congrArg (a ≫ ·) pullback.condition.symm) :
195	        W ⟶ (restrictTest k k').obj (baseTest (k' := k') T))
196	      ≫ coverMap (k' := k') T := by
197	    apply Over.OverMorphism.ext
198	    change Over.Hom.left g = a ≫ pullback.fst T.hom (specMapAlgebra k k')
199	    exact hfac.symm
200	  rw [hgfac]
201	  simp only [op_comp, Functor.map_comp, CategoryTheory.comp_apply, h]
202	
203	/-! ## §3. The input-side transport, and the sharp form of what remains -/
204	
205	/-- **The `k'`-side input, transported: PROVED, and free.**
206	
207	A representation of `picEt` of the **base-changed curve** `C_{k'}` by a
208	`k'`-scheme `X'` is the same thing as a representation of `picEt C` restricted to
209	`k'`-tests. This is `picEt_crossBaseIso` (input 2 of the repair, closed
210	unconditionally by `Picard/PicEtCrossBase.lean`) fed to
211	`Functor.RepresentableBy.ofIso`.
212	
213	It is recorded because it is the step that makes the assembly's hypothesis
214	*statable in the right variables*: without it the `k'`-scheme that campaign `J5`
215	produces would represent `picEt` of the `k`-curve restricted to `k'`-tests rather
216	than `picEt` of `C_{k'}`, and there would be no functor for the Galois action to
217	act on — a mismatch no green build reveals.
218	
219	No separability or finiteness hypothesis on `k'/k`: the cross-base identification
220	never needed one. -/
221	noncomputable def representableByRestrict_of_baseChange
222	    (C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)))
223	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
224	    {X' : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k'))}
225	    (rep : (picEt (Scheme.baseChangeField C k')).RepresentableBy X') :
226	    ((restrictTest k k').op ⋙ picEt C).RepresentableBy X' :=
227	  rep.ofIso (picEt_crossBaseIso C k')
228	
229	/-- **THE CLASS-LEVEL DESCENT IS COMPLETE AND FREE — both halves, not one.**
230	
231	A *compatible family* of `picEt C`-classes on the field-extension cover of a
232	`k`-test `T` has a **unique** amalgamation. So descent of classes along the cover
233	is settled outright: nothing about it is owed.
234	
235	**This corrects the framing of `picEtRestrictEquiv_of_surjective` below, which is
236	this file's own first attempt.** That lemma says restriction is a bijection *as
237	soon as it is surjective*, and I described surjectivity as "the sharp remaining
238	class-level statement". That is too pessimistic, and it is the same
239	already-in-the-tree error `Picard/EtaleFieldCover.lean` records at its own
240	section 4: the amalgamation property of `picEt` is free at **every** covering
241	sieve, `⊤` included, because it is `PicSharp.etaleSheaf`'s own `Sheaf.cond` pushed
242	through the forgetful functor. Applied at *this* sieve — whose membership witness
243	is what `EtaleFieldCover` contributes — it gives existence as well as uniqueness.
244	
245	So the residue of the descent step is **not** in the sheaf theory at all. It is in
246	the two places this file cannot reach:
247	
248	1. producing the *compatible family* from a Galois-invariant `k'`-class, which is
249	   the Hilbert-90/invariance content of campaign `G1`; and
250	2. the **scheme-level** quotient — turning the descended classes into a `k`-scheme
251	   representing `picEt C` — which is campaign `G2` and is gated on
252	   `AlgebraicJacobian.GaloisDescent.HasGaloisQuotient`.
253	
254	A lane pricing the descent step should budget those two and *nothing* for the
255	sheaf-theoretic halves. -/
256	theorem existsUnique_amalgamation_picEt_fieldCover
257	    [FiniteDimensional k k'] [Algebra.IsSeparable k k']
258	    (C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)))
259	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
260	    (T : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)))
261	    (x : Presieve.FamilyOfElements (picEt C)
262	      (((Sieve.overEquiv T).symm
263	        (Sieve.generate (Presieve.singleton
264	          (pullback.fst T.hom (specMapAlgebra k k'))))) : Presieve T))
265	    (hx : x.Compatible) :
266	    ∃! t : (picEt C).obj (Opposite.op T), x.IsAmalgamation t :=
267	  AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.isSheafFor_picEt_pullback_presieve k' C T x hx
268	
269	/-- **A weaker, single-morphism form: restriction is a bijection once surjective.**
270	
271	Kept because it is the shape a consumer holding one class rather than a family
272	wants, and because its injectivity half (`§2`) is the part that needed proof.
273	`existsUnique_amalgamation_picEt_fieldCover` above is strictly stronger and shows
274	`hsurj` is *not* the sharp residue: read that lemma's docstring before pricing
275	anything from this one.
276	
277	Restriction along the cover `T_{k'} ⟶ T` is a **bijection** on `picEt`-classes as
278	soon as it is surjective, because `§2` supplies injectivity unconditionally.
279	
280	**What this is not.** It is not a discharge. `hsurj` has no producer in this
281	project for any curve and any non-trivial `T`: producing one is the existence half
282	of the descent, campaign `G1`/`G2`, whose gate
283	`AlgebraicJacobian.GaloisDescent.HasGaloisQuotient` is instance-free off the affine
284	locus (`Picard/GaloisQuotientAffineGeneral.lean` discharges it for `[IsAffine X]`
285	only, and the object this route descends is glued). The hypothesis is stated
286	explicitly rather than routed through that class so that an axiom check on any
287	future discharge is meaningful.
288	
289	**Non-vacuity of the statement, not of the hypothesis**: `C` occurs in both the
290	hypothesis and the conclusion, the conclusion is an `Equiv` where the hypothesis is
291	only a surjection, and the injectivity that upgrades one to the other is `§2`'s
292	theorem rather than a projection of `hsurj`. At `k' = k` the cover is an
293	isomorphism and the statement degenerates, which is why `§2` — the half that is
294	proved — is stated for an arbitrary `k'` and carries the load. -/
295	noncomputable def picEtRestrictEquiv_of_surjective
296	    [FiniteDimensional k k'] [Algebra.IsSeparable k k']
297	    (C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)))
298	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
299	    (T : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)))
300	    (hsurj : Function.Surjective
301	      (fun t : (picEt C).obj (Opposite.op T) =>
302	        (picEt C).map (coverMap (k' := k') T).op t)) :
303	    (picEt C).obj (Opposite.op T) ≃
304	      (picEt C).obj (Opposite.op ((restrictTest k k').obj (baseTest (k' := k') T))) :=
305	  Equiv.ofBijective _
306	    ⟨fun _ _ h => picEt_injective_restrict_baseTest (k' := k') C T h, hsurj⟩
307	
308	/-! ## §4. What still stands between this and the seam's clause (1)
309	
310	The seam's clause (1) asks for a `k`-scheme representing `picEt C`. What `§3`
311	establishes is that the *class-level* descent along the field-extension cover is
312	**complete**: a compatible family has a unique amalgamation, both halves free from
313	sheafification once the covering-sieve witness of `Picard/EtaleFieldCover.lean` is
314	in hand. What this file does **not** supply, and therefore leaves open, is two
315	things, neither of them sheaf-theoretic:
316	
317	* producing the compatible family from a Galois-invariant `k'`-class (the
318	  invariance content of campaign `G1`); and
319	* the passage from descended classes to a *representing scheme* over `k` — the
320	  quotient construction itself (campaign `G2`), which produces the `k`-scheme as a
321	  quotient of `X'` by the semilinear Galois action, gated on
322	  `AlgebraicJacobian.GaloisDescent.HasGaloisQuotient`. That gate now has a global
323	  instance on the **affine** locus (`Picard/GaloisQuotientAffineGeneral.lean`,
324	  `ajc-p1`), while the object this route descends is glued, so it still bites.
325	
326	Deliberately **not** stated here as a Lean implication with that passage as a
327	hypothesis: an implication whose antecedent is its own conclusion is `P → P`, and
328	an implication whose antecedent is "the `k`-scheme exists with its properties" is
329	that. The route's remaining obligation is a *construction*, and the place for it is
330	`Picard/FiniteGaloisQuotient.lean`'s gate, where it already sits.
331	
332	So the scoreboard this file was written to complete reads, at HEAD: inputs 1 (the
333	cover), 2 (cross-base), 4 (the `k^s` section) landed; input 3 (the Galois quotient)
334	open, gated, affine half only; and the *goal* they feed now exists — with the
335	class-level half of it **closed**, and the remaining cost entirely in `G1`
336	invariance and the `G2` quotient.
337	-/

9	# Finite separable field extensions are étale covers, and the descent test they give
10	
11	This file supplies the **cover** that the repaired campaign tail `G1`/`G3` needs:
12	`Spec k' ⟶ Spec k` for a finite separable extension `k'/k` is a *singleton étale
13	covering* of `Spec k`, its base change along any `k`-scheme `T` is again one, and
14	the resulting sieve lies in `etaleTopologyOver k` — the site on which
15	`PicScheme.picEt` is a sheaf.
16	
17	## Why this file exists
18	
19	The seam's single open obligation `Scheme.fgaPicardRepresentability`
20	(`Picard/FGAPicRepresentability.lean`) is routed through the Milne–Kollár
21	campaign (`informal/pic-representability-campaign.md`). That campaign builds a
22	representing scheme over a separably closed field (`J1`–`J5`), spreads it to a
23	finite Galois level (`G1`) and descends to `k` (`G3`). Its tail is stated for
24	`picSharp`, and that is where the route is believed to break:
25	`PicScheme.not_exists_representing_picSharp_of_not_isIso`
26	(`Picard/PicEtSubcanonical.lean`) proves that **no** scheme represents
27	`picSharp C` once `picEtComparison C` fails to be an isomorphism.
28	
29	**That is a conditional theorem, and the antecedent is not formalised** — stated
30	plainly because this file's own earlier revision asserted the conclusion flatly.
31	`¬IsIso (picEtComparison C)` is an explicit hypothesis of that theorem, proved for
32	no curve. Kleiman's real conic `u²+v²+w²=0` in `ℙ²_ℝ` meets the *binders*
33	(smooth, proper, geometrically integral, no rational point) and he states the
34	non-representability, but the Lean antecedent — that the comparison genuinely
35	fails there, via `φ*O(1)` and `h⁰` on `ℙ¹_ℂ` — is quoted rather than proved
36	(`PicEtSubcanonical.lean` §4 says so of itself). So the honest form is: *if* the
37	comparison fails for one such curve, `G3`/`G4` target a false statement; and the
38	repair is then to descend `picEt`, which **is** an étale sheaf
39	(`PicScheme.picEt_isSheaf_forget`) — whereas whether `picSharp` fails étale
40	descent is likewise not proved here (`th:cmp` part 1 shows it is at least
41	Zariski-*separated* on these binders).
42	
43	Under that repair the descent step needs `Spec k' ⟶ Spec k` to be an **étale
44	covering** in Mathlib's sense, and nothing in the tree provided that. §1–§3 prove
45	it. §4 records what the sheaf side contributes, which is less than an earlier
46	revision claimed. It is infrastructure, not a discharge:
47	
48	**No `sorry` is closed here, and no antecedent of the seam is witnessed.** What
49	changes is that the cover the restated `G3` quantifies over is now a theorem
50	rather than a hypothesis.
51	
52	## The measurement that motivated the shape of the proofs
53	
54	`Algebra.Etale k k'` does **not** synthesize from
55	`[Algebra.IsSeparable k k'] [Module.Finite k k']`, and neither does
56	`Etale (Spec.map …)`; a lane reading a failing `infer_instance` as an absence
57	would conclude this cover is unavailable. Both are assembled below from theorem
58	forms (`Algebra.FormallyEtale.of_isSeparable`,
59	`Algebra.FinitePresentation.of_finiteType`, `RingHom.etale_algebraMap`,
60	`HasRingHomProperty.Spec_iff`). The *base change* of the cover, by contrast, is
61	free by synthesis — `Etale` and `Surjective` are both stable under base change in
62	Mathlib.
63	
64	The sibling project `Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge-Rebuild` has a
65	character-identical `Algebra.Etale` instance — the *anonymous*
66	`instance : Algebra.Etale K L` at `AlgebraicJacobian/Algebra/EtaleCover.lean:304`,

73	Both hypotheses are load-bearing, measured by dropping each: without
74	`[Algebra.IsSeparable k k']`, and separately without `[Module.Finite k k']`,

81	* `Scheme.surjective_specMap_algebraMap` — and surjective (both spectra are

114	/-! ## §1. The étale algebra structure -/
115	
116	section Algebra
117	
118	variable (k k' : Type u) [Field k] [Field k'] [Algebra k k']
119	  [Algebra.IsSeparable k k'] [Module.Finite k k']
120	
121	/-- **A finite separable field extension is an étale algebra.**
122	
123	Formal étaleness is separability (`Algebra.FormallyEtale.of_isSeparable`), and
124	finite presentation follows from finite type over a field
125	(`Algebra.FinitePresentation.of_finiteType`, the Noetherian criterion).
126	
127	Stated as an `instance` because both inputs are, and because
128	`Algebra.Etale k k'` does *not* synthesize without it: this is the declaration
129	whose absence makes the étale cover below look unavailable. -/
130	instance etale_of_finite_isSeparable : Algebra.Etale k k' where
131	  formallyEtale := Algebra.FormallyEtale.of_isSeparable k k'
132	  finitePresentation :=
133	    (Algebra.FinitePresentation.of_finiteType (R := k) (A := k')).mp inferInstance
134	
135	end Algebra

137	/-! ## §2. The scheme-level cover -/
138	
139	section Cover
140	
141	variable (k k' : Type u) [Field k] [Field k'] [Algebra k k']
142	
143	/-- **`Spec k' ⟶ Spec k` is surjective on points**, for *any* extension of
144	fields: both spectra have exactly one point, so this needs neither separability
145	nor finiteness.
146	
147	Stated on the underlying map because that is the form
148	`Scheme.singleton_mem_precoverage_iff` consumes; the morphism-property version is
149	`surjective_specMap_algebraMap` below. -/
150	theorem surjective_base_specMap_algebraMap :
151	    Function.Surjective (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k k'))).base :=
152	  fun _ => ⟨default, Subsingleton.elim _ _⟩
153	
154	/-- `Spec k' ⟶ Spec k` is surjective as a morphism property. -/
155	theorem surjective_specMap_algebraMap :
156	    Surjective (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k k'))) :=
157	  ⟨surjective_base_specMap_algebraMap k k'⟩
158	
159	variable [Algebra.IsSeparable k k'] [Module.Finite k k']
160	
161	/-- **`Spec k' ⟶ Spec k` is étale** for `k'/k` finite separable.
162	
163	The bridge from the algebra statement of §1 to the morphism property is
164	`RingHom.etale_algebraMap` followed by `HasRingHomProperty.Spec_iff`. It is
165	needed because `Etale (Spec.map …)` does not synthesize: `RingHom.Etale f` is
166	`Algebra.Etale` at `f.toAlgebra`, which is not the ambient `Algebra k k'`
167	instance up to reducible defeq. -/
168	theorem etale_specMap_algebraMap :
169	    Etale (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k k'))) :=
170	  (HasRingHomProperty.Spec_iff (P := @Etale)).mpr
171	    (RingHom.etale_algebraMap.mpr inferInstance)
172	
173	/-- **The singleton family `{Spec k' ⟶ Spec k}` is an étale cover of `Spec k`.**
174	
175	`Scheme.singleton_mem_precoverage_iff` reduces membership in the étale
176	precoverage to exactly the two facts above: surjectivity on points, and the
177	morphism property. -/
178	theorem singleton_mem_etalePrecoverage_specMap :
179	    Presieve.singleton (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k k'))) ∈
180	      Scheme.precoverage @Etale (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)) := by
181	  rw [Scheme.singleton_mem_precoverage_iff]
182	  exact ⟨surjective_base_specMap_algebraMap k k', etale_specMap_algebraMap k k'⟩
183	
184	/-- The sieve generated by the field-extension cover is a **covering sieve** of
185	the big étale topology on schemes. This is the form the sheaf axiom of
186	`PicSharp.etaleSheaf` is stated against. -/
187	theorem sieve_specMap_mem_etaleTopology :
188	    Sieve.generate
189	        (Presieve.singleton (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k k')))) ∈
190	      Scheme.etaleTopology (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)) :=
191	  Precoverage.generate_mem_toGrothendieck (singleton_mem_etalePrecoverage_specMap k k')
192	
193	end Cover

198	
199	variable (k k' : Type u) [Field k] [Field k'] [Algebra k k']
200	  [Algebra.IsSeparable k k'] [Module.Finite k k']
201	
202	/-- **The base-changed cover is étale.** `Etale` is stable under base change in

204	no argument beyond §2 — recorded because it is the form `G1`'s spreading step

206	theorem etale_pullback_fst_specMap (T : Scheme.{u}) (a : T ⟶ Spec (CommRingCat.of k)) :
207	    Etale (pullback.fst a (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k k')))) :=
208	  haveI := etale_specMap_algebraMap k k'
209	  inferInstance

211	omit [Algebra.IsSeparable k k'] [Module.Finite k k'] in

213	with `etale_pullback_fst_specMap` this says the field-extension cover pulls back

216	Needs neither separability nor finiteness, for the same reason
217	`surjective_base_specMap_algebraMap` does not. -/
218	theorem surjective_pullback_fst_specMap (T : Scheme.{u})
219	    (a : T ⟶ Spec (CommRingCat.of k)) :
220	    Surjective (pullback.fst a (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k k')))) :=

226	/-! ## §4. The descent test for `picEt` -/
227	
228	section Descent
229	
230	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] (k' : Type u) [Field k'] [Algebra k k']
231	  [Algebra.IsSeparable k k'] [Module.Finite k k']
232	
233	/-- The base-changed cover, as an étale cover of the *underlying scheme* of a
234	slice object `T`. Restatement of §3 in presieve form. -/
235	theorem singleton_pullback_mem_etalePrecoverage (T : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))) :
236	    Presieve.singleton
237	        (pullback.fst T.hom (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k k')))) ∈
238	      Scheme.precoverage @Etale T.left := by
239	  haveI := etale_specMap_algebraMap k k'
240	  haveI : Surjective (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k k'))) :=
241	    surjective_specMap_algebraMap k k'
242	  rw [Scheme.singleton_mem_precoverage_iff]
243	  exact ⟨Surjective.surj
244	    (f := pullback.fst T.hom (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k k')))),
245	    inferInstance⟩
246	
247	/-- **The field-extension cover, transported into the site `(Sch/k)`** on which
248	the relative Picard presheaf lives.
249	
250	`etaleTopologyOver k` is `Scheme.etaleTopology.over (Spec k)`, whose covering
251	sieves are by definition those whose image under `Sieve.overEquiv` covers the
252	underlying scheme; `GrothendieckTopology.overEquiv_symm_mem_over` is that
253	definition read backwards. -/
254	theorem sieve_pullback_mem_etaleTopologyOver (T : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))) :
255	    (Sieve.overEquiv T).symm
256	        (Sieve.generate (Presieve.singleton
257	          (pullback.fst T.hom (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k k')))))) ∈
258	      etaleTopologyOver k T :=
259	  GrothendieckTopology.overEquiv_symm_mem_over (J := Scheme.etaleTopology) T _
260	    (Precoverage.generate_mem_toGrothendieck
261	      (singleton_pullback_mem_etalePrecoverage k' T))
262	
263	/-- **The sheaf axiom of `picEt` at an arbitrary covering sieve.**
264	
265	This is `PicScheme.picEt_isSheaf_forget` (`Picard/PicEtSheaf.lean`) unfolded at
266	one sieve, and it is stated here to make the division of labour explicit: the
267	sheaf property is **free** — it is `PicSharp.etaleSheaf`'s own `Sheaf.cond`,
268	pushed through the forgetful functor — and holds at *every* covering sieve of
269	`etaleTopologyOver k`, the trivial sieve `⊤` included. Nothing about a field
270	extension enters.
271	
272	An earlier revision of this file proved the sheaf property again here, by a
273	different route (`Presheaf.isSheaf_iff_isSheaf_forget` in place of
274	`sheafCompose`), and presented it as new work. It was already in this file's
275	import closure; the duplicate is deleted rather than annotated. What §1–§3
276	contribute is not the sheaf axiom but a **particular covering sieve** that the
277	campaign's descent step needs and that the tree did not have. -/
278	theorem isSheafFor_picEt_of_mem (C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)))
279	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
280	    {T : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))} (S : Sieve T)
281	    (hS : S ∈ etaleTopologyOver k T) :
282	    Presieve.IsSheafFor (PicScheme.picEt C) (S : Presieve T) :=
283	  PicScheme.picEt_isSheaf_forget C S hS
284	
285	/-- **The sheaf axiom of `picEt` at the field-extension cover.**
286	
287	Concretely: for a `k`-scheme `T` and a finite separable `k'/k`, a family of
288	`Pic_{(C/k)ét}`-classes on `T ×_k k'` that is compatible on overlaps has a
289	*unique* amalgamation on `T`. No hypothesis on `C(k)` anywhere.
290	
291	**Where the content is, stated precisely because an earlier revision of this
292	docstring got it wrong.** That revision called this "THE DESCENT TEST" and "the
293	payoff", implying the sheaf side was the achievement. It is not: by
294	`isSheafFor_picEt_of_mem` the amalgamation property holds at *every* covering
295	sieve, `⊤` included, for free from sheafification. The only thing this
296	declaration adds over that is the *membership witness* — that this particular
297	family, the one the campaign's descent step actually restricts along, is a
298	covering sieve. That witness is §1–§3, and it is what the tree lacked.
299	
300	**What it does not give, and this is the larger half.** A descent *test* is not a
301	descended object. Turning a `k'`-representing scheme into a `k`-representing one
302	needs the semilinear Galois action and the effectivity of the resulting descent
303	datum — campaign `G1`/`G2`, `Picard/FiniteGaloisQuotient.lean`, whose existence
304	gate `HasGaloisQuotient` is discharged only for an **affine** total space
305	(`Picard/GaloisQuotientAffineGeneral.lean`, 2026-07-30) while the object this route
306	descends is glued, so the gate still bites here. So this closes no `sorry` and
307	witnesses no antecedent of `Scheme.fgaPicardRepresentability`. -/
308	theorem isSheafFor_picEt_pullback_presieve (C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)))
309	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
310	    (T : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))) :
311	    Presieve.IsSheafFor (PicScheme.picEt C)
312	      (((Sieve.overEquiv T).symm
313	        (Sieve.generate (Presieve.singleton
314	          (pullback.fst T.hom
315	            (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k k'))))))) : Presieve T) :=
316	  isSheafFor_picEt_of_mem C _ (sieve_pullback_mem_etaleTopologyOver k' T)
317	
318	/-- **The separatedness half, in the form `G3` uses it: restriction along the
319	cover is injective on `picEt`-classes.**
320	
321	Two classes in `Pic_{(C/k)ét}(T)` that agree after restriction along the
322	base-changed field-extension cover are *equal*. This is the direction the
323	Hilbert-90 step of campaign `G3` consumes — it is what makes an invariant class
324	determined by its `k'`-shadow, so that a descent datum is unique once it exists.
325	
326	It is strictly weaker than `isSheafFor_picEt_pullback_presieve` (separatedness is
327	the uniqueness half of the sheaf axiom) and is recorded separately because it is
328	the half that is used on its own. The corresponding statement for `picSharp` is
329	*not* known to fail — `th:cmp` part 1 gives `picSharp ↪ Pic_{(C/k)zar}` on these
330	binders — so it is the *amalgamation* half above, not this one, that the repair

332	theorem picEt_ext_of_pullback_agrees (C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)))
333	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
334	    (T : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)))
335	    {t₁ t₂ : (PicScheme.picEt C).obj (Opposite.op T)}
336	    (h : ∀ ⦃W : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))⦄ ⦃g : W ⟶ T⦄,
337	      (((Sieve.overEquiv T).symm
338	        (Sieve.generate (Presieve.singleton
339	          (pullback.fst T.hom
340	            (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k k'))))))) : Presieve T) g →
341	      (PicScheme.picEt C).map g.op t₁ = (PicScheme.picEt C).map g.op t₂) :
342	    t₁ = t₂ :=
343	  (isSheafFor_picEt_pullback_presieve k' C T).isSeparatedFor.ext h
